jobs.prompt: Every job in reviewed snapshot {version} ({date}) has passed fact and three-language review. The default list shows only the records that are still listable now: confirmed-closed and expired records stay in the archive, and records whose application window has passed drop out of the default list, so the result count shown with the filters is the real number. Postdoctoral posts are not a separate result set and are in the default list; use the master's-eligible filter to narrow by degree threshold. This is not every school vacancy: new candidates require degree, doctoral-enrolment, pay-status and language review first.

guides.title: Application guides
guides.intro: This site helps you research study programmes and research or doctoral opportunities. Applications must be submitted by you through the official university or employer channel.
guides.body: Choose the language of instruction first, then check admission language evidence, extra language needs for placements or clinics, tuition terms, and the current application round. A CSCSE lookup is a reference, not a personal recognition guarantee. Research jobs use working language and doctoral enrollment filters, not teaching-language filters.
guides.s1.title: Step 1: choose the language of instruction
guides.s1.body: Study programmes are split by language of instruction first: English and Czech sit side by side at that first level, and no university, degree or ranking replaces it. The interface language only changes the page text; it never turns your programme preference into Czech or English. Once a language of instruction is selected, the list shows programmes taught in it. Tick “include programmes requiring both languages” only when you also want programmes that require English and Czech.
guides.s2.title: Rounds and deadlines
guides.s2.body: A programme detail page lists every verified application round on a timeline and highlights the round that currently applies. An unpublished start date does not mean applications are open, and rolling applications are labelled as such. “Open only if vacancies remain” means a supplementary round depends on remaining places and is not marked open before that is confirmed; when a whole opportunity is closed, none of its rounds accept applications. Sort by deadline to see what expires soonest, and confirm the range with the “applications open” status.
guides.s3.title: How tuition is stated
guides.s3.body: The tuition field states the billing cycle (year / semester / whole programme) and the currency, taken from the official page or the Ministry of Education register. “Tuition not published” is neither free nor 0, and it is never filtered as 0. An application fee is a separate charge and is not merged with tuition into one figure. For register records, tuition appears only where a university source proves it; otherwise it stays unknown.
guides.s4.title: English-taught programmes can still require Czech
guides.s4.body: The detail page separates admission language evidence from additional required languages. Czech may also be required for clinical work, placements or practical training, and each entry is marked required, optional or not published; where evidence is missing, the site does not conclude that nothing is required. A research post’s working language is a separate measure and is never filtered by language of instruction.
guides.s5.title: Research and doctoral posts: threshold, enrollment and pay
guides.s5.body: The job list shows every published position by default, postdoctoral posts included, and the research entry does not require a teaching-language choice first. The type of post, the education threshold and compensation are three separate facts in a vacancy, and none of them stands in for another.
guides.s6.title: Ownership and the CSCSE reference
guides.s6.body: Institution tags show ownership and the CSCSE reference side by side. Both are references only: neither guarantees personal recognition, and neither “public” nor any ranking replaces the lookup result.
guides.s7.title: Timeliness and the limits of this site
guides.s7.body: Every record states its source class, collection date and fact-review date, and the default sort puts verified, open opportunities first. This site has no accounts, no saved items and no comparison; it does not submit applications for you and does not predict admission odds.

map.title: Institution map
map.intro: The map is an auxiliary view; the list is the data. The default view is the bundled Czech map: 14 regions, major cities, and waterways. Zoom with the wheel or buttons, and pan by dragging. It does not depend on Google Maps or foreign map tiles.
map.disclaimer: Identity stays on the ministry register. Coordinates prefer Wikidata P625 when IČO, website host, or the official Czech name matches uniquely; otherwise the register seat is geocoded with Nominatim. Missing points are not invented. At low zoom the interactive view groups nearby schools into keyboard-operable count buttons; zooming in restores a separate button for each school, with exactly coincident pins slightly spread around their source coordinate. Use the list to verify the school. The CSCSE name “College of Political and Social Sciences” is not on the current register, so it is not plotted.
